issues.detail: Error handling is mostly limited to a note on validation retries and a usage-limit tip; it does not cover provider errors, rate limits, timeouts, or what to do when retries are exhausted (UnexpectedModelBehavior).

scenarios.name: typed-extraction-with-current-names
scenarios.rationale: Both meet every rubric point: BaseModel with typed fields, `output_type=`, `result.output`, `run_sync` and a `provider:model-id` string. A uses `openai:gpt-5`, the rubric's own example. B uses `anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5`, which is also a valid format, and it adds currency, Decimal and retries. A matches the rubric example more closely, so it scores slightly higher.

scenarios.name: tool-with-deps-and-usage-limit
scenarios.rationale: Both meet every rubric item (deps dataclass, `deps_type=`, `@agent.tool` with `ctx: RunContext`, docstring, `deps=` and `usage_limits=UsageLimits(request_limit=...)` in the run call, narrow argument types), but B adds `tool_calls_limit` and `total_tokens_limit`, typed `int` ids, retry handling, and a `UsageLimitExceeded` fallback in code, while A only mentions catching the exception and uses a loosely typed `dict` return with a string-quoted `Database` type.

scenarios.name: offline-test-and-streaming
scenarios.rationale: Response A follows the rubric: it streams with run_stream and stream_text(delta=True), prints each chunk, and tests with agent.override(model=TestModel()) imported from pydantic_ai.models.test. Response B streams correctly but tests with FunctionModel, and mentions TestModel only as an aside, so it misses the rubric's required test approach.
